issues.legal_issue: Whether tax authorities could go behind a conveyance and independently allocate the purchase price for depreciation purposes was a question of law requiring reference to the High Court.
material_facts: The purchaser paid the full purchase price stated in the sale deed, which allocated part of the consideration to machinery and related assets.
The income-tax authorities and the Tribunal allocated part of that consideration to goodwill, although the sale deed did not separately mention a sale of goodwill.
The purchaser challenged the authorities’ competence to go behind the conveyance and fix their own valuation.
The Tribunal declined to refer the question, and the High Court declined to direct a reference.
issues.conclusion: The question whether the Income-tax Officer was competent, on these facts, to go behind the conveyance and fix a valuation of his own was a question of law that should have been referred to the High Court. The Court did not decide the substantive valuation question.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 66(1) and 66(2) of the Indian Income-tax Act, a question of law arising from the Tribunal’s order may be referred to the High Court. Section 10(2)(vi) provides for depreciation by reference to the original cost to the assessee; Commissioner of Income-tax v. Buckingham & Carnatic Co. Ltd. was relied on for the principle that this means the cost to the assessee, not the predecessor. The Court held that the authorities’ competence to go behind the conveyance raised a question of law, but expressly left unresolved whether the English authorities or the Lahore High Court approach governed that substantive issue.

predicates.income_tax_depreciation_reference_procee: The proceeding concerns a request for a High Court reference arising from an income-tax depreciation assessment.
predicates.purchase_price_stated_in_conveyance: The purchaser paid a price stated in a conveyance that allocated consideration among the transferred assets.
predicates.tax_authorities_reallocated_consideratio: The tax authorities allocated some of the stated consideration to an asset not separately identified in the conveyance.
predicates.assessee_contested_authority_to_disregar: The assessee disputed the tax authorities’ competence to disregard the conveyance’s allocation and make their own valuation.

issues.definition: When a depreciation-reference proceeding involves a stated conveyance price that tax authorities reallocate and the assessee contests their authority to do so, the authority question requires reference to the High Court.
